summary: Synthesis gave 736 cells and 8363.0208 um2. Setup is met at all three corners; the worst is nom_ss_100C_1v60 at 3.720212 ns (path baud_div[0] to flip-flop _1296_, dominated by a high-fanout o41ai_2 gate, 2.396546 ns). Hold is -0.002920 ns at nom_ff_n40C_1v95, which needs follow-up. No eqy data was provided.
assumptions: All numbers come from reports/synth_tool.json as given; I ran no tools.
Ideal clocks are assumed pre-layout, as stated in the SDC and the report (clock network delay ideal).
Statements about what the baud_div logic does (zero-detect or counter reload) are my inference from the path shape and the spec, not tool output.
The worst_paths_report text is truncated, so only paths 1 and 2 are fully readable; the slack of path 3 is not quoted.
open_issues: Hold slack is negative (-0.002920 ns) at nom_ff_n40C_1v95 pre-layout. The hold path is not in the data. A human or PnR agent must decide how to handle it (for example hold repair after CTS); I have not waived or loosened anything.
No equivalence (eqy) result was provided, so RTL-to-netlist equivalence is unproven and remains blocking.

Several paths fan out from baud_div[0] through a high-fanout o41ai_2 (fanout 24, slew 2.745 ns). Timing is met with margin at 20 ns, but this may be worth a look if the clock target is tightened. This is not a fix request.
The worst paths report is truncated: paths 3 to 10, and the paths for the tt and ff corners, are not visible.
rx is constrained with the 30% default input delay and no false path, as the SDC notes; the human decision on its treatment is still open.

self_assessment.reason: Quoted numbers match the tool data exactly, but the path report is truncated, there is no eqy or hold-path detail, and the functional reading of the path is an inference.
